questions.text: What does the LORD say in Malachi 1:2-3 concerning his love?

options.text: I loved Esau, and I hated Jacob
I loved Jacob, and I hated Esau
I loved both of them equally
I loved only the holy priests

questions.text: What profanation did the LORD charge upon the priests in Malachi 1:7-8?

options.text: They offered strange incense and poured out drink offerings unto idols
They neglected the sacrifices and refused to bring the tithes of the flock
They offered the blind, the lame, and the sick upon the altar of the LORD
They sacrificed in secret places, far from the sanctuary and the temple

questions.text: What promise is given in Malachi 1:11?

options.text: My name shall be forgotten among the heathen from the rising of the sun
Only in Jerusalem shall my name be great, but the Gentiles will mock it
My name shall be hidden from all people, and the nations shall not know me
From the rising of the sun unto the going down my name shall be great

questions.text: How was God's covenant with Levi described in Malachi 2:5-6?

options.text: A covenant of life and peace; the law of truth was in his mouth
A covenant of power and gold; the sword of justice was in his hand
A covenant of fasting and tears; the prayer of sorrow was on his lips
A covenant of kings and armies; the victory of battle was with him

questions.text: What does the LORD say in Malachi 2:16 concerning marriage?

options.text: He commandeth putting away when contention ariseth in the house
He hateth putting away, and one should not deal treacherously
He permiteth putting away if the vows of youth are broken
He looketh not upon marriage, for it is only an earthly thing

questions.text: How had the people wearied the LORD according to Malachi 2:17?

options.text: By crying continually unto God for deliverance from their heathen masters
By building altars unto strange gods in the valleys and on high hills
By saying: Every one that doeth evil is good in the sight of the LORD
By refusing to bring their children unto the priest to be blessed in Zion

questions.text: Who shall come according to Malachi 3:1?

options.text: A mighty conqueror of the heathen who shall overthrow all foreign kingdoms
The prophet Moses who shall write the holy commandments once more in Zion
An angel with a drawn sword who shall judge the wicked and their idols
The messenger of the covenant, and the Lord shall come to his temple

questions.text: With what imagery does Malachi 3:2-3 describe the messenger of the covenant?

options.text: Like a refiner's fire and fullers' soap; he shall purify the sons of Levi
Like a storm and earthquake breaking the mountains, breaking the priests
Like a sword and shield smiting the enemies, so shall he judge all nations
Like a shepherd searching the lost sheep, so shall he prove all the people

questions.text: Wherein had the people robbed God according to Malachi 3:8?

options.text: In their neglect of the daily morning and evening prayer in the temple
In tithes and offerings; they should bring all into the storehouse
In their refusal to fast and mourn in the fifth and seventh months
In selling the holy vessels of the sanctuary unto foreign merchants

questions.text: How is the coming day described in Malachi 4:1?

options.text: It shall come with thick darkness, and the earth shall shake with fear
It shall come like an overflowing flood, and all towers shall fall down
It shall burn as an oven, and all the proud and wicked shall be stubble
It shall come with heavy tempest, and hail shall destroy all the trees

questions.text: What shall arise unto them that fear the name of the LORD in Malachi 4:2?

options.text: The morning star of glory with riches for the poor
The light of wisdom with understanding for the elders
The dawn of victory with deliverance for the captive
The Sun of righteousness with healing in his wings

questions.text: With what promise does the Old Testament conclude (Malachi 4:5-6)?

options.text: The LORD will send Elijah the prophet before the great day of the LORD
A new temple shall be built in Jerusalem before the final end of all time
A righteous king of David's line shall arise before judgment upon nations
All heathen kingdoms shall bring their wealth before the throne of God

questions.text: What does the LORD ask the priests that despise his name in Malachi 1:6?

options.text: If I be a father, where is mine honour? and if a master, where is my fear?
If I be the Creator, where are your offerings and the tithes of your flock?
If I be your King, where is your obedience and the service of your hands?
If I be your Shepherd, where are the lost sheep of the house of Israel?

questions.text: Whom does the LORD curse in Malachi 1:14?

options.text: The priest who profaneth the holy sabbath and refuseth to teach the people
The deceiver who hath a male, yet voweth and sacrificeth a corrupt thing
The ruler who oppresseth the poor and taketh away their inheritance
The merchant who useth false balances and cheateth the stranger in Zion

questions.text: What should the priest's lips keep according to Malachi 2:7?

options.text: Gold and treasures of the sanctuary for the poor
The secrets of the holy temple and the holy things
Knowledge, for he is the messenger of the LORD
Praise and thanksgiving before the golden altar

questions.text: Which two questions does Malachi 2:10 ask the people?

options.text: Hath not every tribe its own inheritance?
Is not the father greater than the son?
Hath not one God created us of old?
Have we not all one father in heaven?

questions.text: Against whom will the LORD be a swift witness in Malachi 3:5?

options.text: Against the sorcerers and the adulterers
Against the heathen who spoil the temple
Against the rulers who lead men to war
Against those that oppress the fatherless

questions.text: What does the LORD say of himself in Malachi 3:6?

options.text: I am the LORD, and I have withdrawn myself
I am the LORD, and I alter my holy covenant
I am the LORD, and I remember your iniquities
I am the LORD, I change not for evermore

questions.text: What was written before the LORD for them that feared him (Malachi 3:16)?

options.text: A book of remembrance for them that feared the LORD and thought upon his name
A memorial stone for them that built the sanctuary and adorned the altar
A scroll of judgment for them that despised the commandment and mocked God
A covenant of peace for them that brought their tithes and offered sacrifices

questions.text: How shall they that fear the LORD go forth according to Malachi 4:2?

options.text: They shall walk quietly and stand firm as the tall cedars
They shall go forth and grow up as the calves of the stall
They shall rest and lie down satisfied like sheep in pasture
They shall run swiftly and fly upward as the young eagles
